_purpose: A path that names nothing is refused, not accepted as null. Spawning a class that does not exist, reading a property off an asset that does not exist, writing an object reference from a bad path, and passing one as a function argument are all rejected with the path quoted back. The failure this guards against is the quiet one: the reference resolves to nothing, the call reports success, and the damage shows up somewhere else entirely - a material instance with no parent rendering black with nothing in the log.
_reading: Every rejection here carries expect_failure:true, so a correct run reads green. A step that is allowed through is the bug.

steps._why: Clear the probe an aborted earlier run may have left behind. Deleting nothing is not an error.

steps._note: A Blueprint class path no asset backs. This must not spawn an empty actor and call it done.
The same failure from a different source: a native class path with a typo in it.
The target itself does not resolve - nothing to read a property from.
The target resolves and the property does not. The error names the class it looked on, which is the half a caller cannot guess.

Owner is a real object reference on this actor and it is currently empty - an unset reference reads back as an empty path, not as an invented one. That makes the refusal below a statement about the path rather than about the property.

The one that matters: an object-typed property handed a path that resolves to nothing. The engine's own text import accepts this, stores null and reports success - set_property checks the result and refuses instead.
The same guard on the argument side. Passing a silently-null asset into a function is how a wrong result gets blamed on the function instead of on the path that was typed.
An actor name that matches nothing. The error lists what is actually in the world, because the usual cause is a label/name mismatch or the wrong world.
And the asset-shaped version of the same mistake: an edit aimed at a Blueprint that is not there.
